definitions.denominator: every product certification issued in the run
definitions.name: false_product_certification_rate
definitions.numerator: certifications in which a product property was reported SUPPORTED while the ground-truth scenario had removed a dependency that property declares
definitions.trap: A system that certifies nothing scores 0.0. Never read it without product_coverage beside it.
definitions.why: It is THE number. Every other metric here is about how much the system delivers; this one is about whether what it delivers can be believed.

definitions.name: false_product_certification_count
definitions.numerator: the same set, counted rather than divided
definitions.why: A rate of 0.01 over 100 trials and over 10000 trials are not the same evidence, and a table showing only the rate lets them look identical.

definitions.denominator: products declared in the contract set
definitions.name: product_coverage
definitions.numerator: products whose assurance result lists at least one supported quality property
definitions.trap: A product with one supported property counts the same as one with five. Use assured_mission_yield for the graded view.
definitions.why: The counterweight to the false-certification rate. Together they say whether the system is both honest AND useful; either alone can be satisfied by a system that is one and not the other.

definitions.formula: sum over products of (supported_properties / declared_properties) / products_declared
definitions.name: assured_mission_yield
definitions.numerator: per-product fraction of properties supported, summed
definitions.trap: It weights every property and every product equally, which no real mission does. It is a benchmark number, not a mission value function, and must not be optimised against.
definitions.why: The product principle is MAXIMIZE ASSURANCE-QUALIFIED USEFUL INFORMATION. This is the closest thing to a direct measurement of it: partial products count partially.

definitions.name: capability_recovery_latency
definitions.numerator: not applicable -- a duration per capability per event
definitions.trap: Lower is NOT better. Reporting it with a 'lower is better' arrow would reward the exact defect it detects.
definitions.why: It is expected to be POSITIVE and non-trivial. A latency near zero means the system restored a capability on presence rather than on re-established evidence, which is BAD_PRODUCT_05.

definitions.name: unsupported_planner_request_count
definitions.trap: Neither direction is good. It is a liveness check on the gate, not a score.
definitions.why: A non-zero count means the gate is doing work. Zero across a degradation scenario means either the planner never tried anything ambitious or the gate is not wired in.

definitions.formula: |certificates that expired while still being consulted|
definitions.name: certificate_expiry_events
definitions.numerator: reads of a certificate after its expires_at
definitions.why: Every one is a place where stale support could have leaked into a decision. It should be zero, and if it is not, the individual events are more interesting than the total.
